decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Discount Rates in Mineral Rights DCF: A Plain-Language Guide
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 787870b5263f66eed90e1cafe4b568f59580adf3f576f01c58dfe3cd1251688d; all 7 declared official sources passed live access review.
Rate consistency, standardized reserve disclosure, Treasury market-reference, regulatory production-data, and public property-appraisal claims remain bounded to their official government sources.

The article uses no fabricated owners, wells, leases, production, forecasts, prices, costs, rates, reserves, transaction values, market evidence, testimonials, or owner-specific legal, tax, investment, reserve, engineering, or valuation conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Business Valuation Guidelines, IRM 4.48.4 (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The IRS Business Valuation Guidelines state that an appraiser should select a benefit stream and discount or capitalization rate consistent with the selected valuation method and consider relevant risk factors.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the guidelines only for a general valuation-consistency principle; it does not present the IRS material as a mineral-property formula, owner-specific appraisal, tax conclusion, or universal rate.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic 12: Oil and Gas Producing Activities (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic 12 explains that U.S. GAAP requires disclosure of the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows from production of proved oil-and-gas reserves.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses this material only to identify the specified reporting context; it does not equate that measure with a private mineral-owner offer, fair market value, or an owner-specific DCF.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Accounting and Reporting for Oil and Gas Producing Activities, Release No. 33-10002 (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The SEC release describes the standardized measure as after-tax future net cash flows discounted at 10 percent and notes that the standardized measure is neither fair market value nor the present value of expected future cash flows.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the release to distinguish a prescribed disclosure convention from owner-specific valuation and does not claim that 10 percent is appropriate for a particular mineral interest.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The U.S. Treasury publishes daily par yield curves derived from indicative market quotations for Treasury securities at fixed maturities.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses Treasury data only as dated market-reference context and does not treat a Treasury yield as a complete mineral-rights discount rate or owner-specific conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Production Data (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas publishes production compilations and summaries based on information reported to the Commission by operators and provides multiple production-query and download paths.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page to identify a public regulatory production source and does not treat reported production as a complete owner cash flow, reserve report, or forecast.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Production Data Query System FAQs (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission explains that Texas oil production may be reported at the lease level, online production information has a reporting lag, and records can change as corrected, revised, or delinquent reports arrive.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses these limitations to bound production-history work and does not infer individual-well volumes, payment ownership, title, or future production from a regulatory record.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Comptroller, Valuing Property (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Comptroller describes the sales-comparison, income, and cost approaches and explains that the income approach estimates the present worth of anticipated future benefits.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article preserves the public property-tax context and does not present the page as a private-sale formula, professional appraisal, title conclusion, or owner-specific value.
